Our Secondary School, also known as ‘The Ark’ is located in Frome & offers a supportive learning environment.

For any other information please contact our Headteacher Ben Coombes on 07551 057828/ ben.coombes@enhancedlearningservices.co.uk

We are an Ofsted graded GOOD school and are proud to be named as a Trauma Informed school, with all staff specifically trained in these areas. We are an independent SEMH school offering an individualised education to improve life outcomes.
Our team of staff provide highly specialised education provision and support to students who have complex needs. Our school runs across three sites, the Ark in Frome and Newmead Farm in Maiden Bradley & our new Primary School site in Kilmington.
We are passionate about providing excellent, bespoke education and opportunities for our students. Our four pillar goals are CARE – care, adaptability, resilience and empathy; through these we develop our students social, moral, spiritual and cultural skills, and add to this academic achievement, developing our young people so that they can secure, safe and contributing members of society.
As a Trauma informed school everything we do is Trauma Informed. Students thrive and progress in our school, and their attainment, engagement and progress is significantly higher in comparison to previous placements, as recognised by OFSTED. We are extremely proud of our school, our students and our amazing staff.
Education
We provide high quality, holistic care and learning to improve the lives of children and young people through a proven range of practitioner-led services.
Clinical
We aim to provide our students with a safe, caring and nurturing community with clear, consistent boundaries and high expectations. Relationships are at the heart of our approach and are based on sensitive understanding of a young person’s experiences and the areas in which they require more support.

Home Our Approach Careers
Careers
‘Supporting students to prepare for their future, their way’
At Wessex Lodge School we aim to provide an individualised education to improve life outcomes. We recognise that supporting students to find the right pathway for them is a large part of this. Choosing which direction to take after leaving school is a big decision. We’re here to support our students and make sure they know all the options and routes open to them. Our Careers programme is designed to give our young people the skills, knowledge and confidence they require to find and access a career they will enjoy and thrive in.
Using the Gatsby Benchmarks and CDI Framework as a guide and Careerpilot and The Princes Trust Personal Development and Employability Skills qualification materials as a source we have created a careers programme for all students that can be individualised to meet their needs. Alongside dedicated careers lessons students will receive advise from an independent, level 6 Careers Advisor on request.
The Careers Lead is Laura Gregg: LauraG@enhancedlearningservices.co.uk 01985844865
Our Futures Advisor (Careers Advisor) is Oli Masters: oli.masters@ofgl.co.uk
The Gatsby benchmarks are seen as best practice for careers guidance within schools. We use Gatsby benchmarks to measure our program and complete termly Compass evaluations. The Gatsby benchmarks are:
1 Stable careers programme
2 Learning from career and labour market information
3 Addressing the needs of each pupil
4 Linking curriculum learning to careers
5 Encounters with employers and employees
6 Experiences of work places
7 Encounters with Further and Higher Education
Compass Evaluations:
Our next review will be completed Summer 2025.
Our full careers programme for the 24-25 academic year can be found below. The Incredible Futures Careers Programme was created incorporating the CDI Framework into the programme. More information on the framework can be found here: https://www.thecdi.net/New-Career-Development-Framework
Information on The Princes Trust Personal Development and Employability Skills qualification can be found here: https://www.princes-trust.org.uk/about-us/qualifications/personal-development-and-employability-skills-2021
We have access to Careerpilot, which can be used as a source of information during Careers lessons. There is a parent zone on their website filled with lots of useful information, which can be found here: https://www.careerpilot.org.uk/parent-zone
Other useful websites include:
The National Careers Service: https://nationalcareers.service.gov.uk/
Talking Futures: https://www.talkingfutures.org.uk/
Amazing Apprenticeships: https://amazingapprenticeships.com/
Icould: https://icould.com/
The information on this page will be reviewed in Summer 2025.

Home About Us Senior Leadership Team
Ben Coombes
Headteacher
Stuart Hamilton Deputy Head Stuart Hamilton is a committed and compassionate Deputy Head who has been working in Education for over 30 years, with extensive experience in pastoral care, safeguarding, and supporting students with Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs. Based at Newmead farm, Stuart plays a pivotal role in creating a safe, inclusive, and nurturing school environment where every student feels valued and supported. His calm and strategic leadership style, combined with a deep understanding of the challenges young people face, enables him to lead with empathy and impact. Stuart is passionate about promoting wellbeing across the school community and works closely with staff, families, and external agencies to ensure the best outcomes for all learners. Nigel Troop Assistant Headteacher/ Deputy Safeguarding Lead Nigel has worked with children with early life trauma for over 40 years in a variety of settings. He started his career as a residential worker and then moved into teaching 35 years ago, after completing his PGCE at Goldsmiths. He has worked in a variety of settings including residential SEMH schools, pupil referral units and independent special schools. In addition he managed provision for vulnerable students in a mainstream setting for a number of years. He has worked as a senior teacher, Deputy Head and Head teacher during the course of his career and currently is Assistant Head at WLS with previous responsibility for leading the Safeguarding team. Despite cutting down on his work commitments in recent times, He remains committed to the ethos of creating a school environment that is inclusive, child centred and safe for all our students. Bethany Vowles Assistant Headteacher – The Ark After working in mainstream education for 9 years Bethany moved into the SEMH sector. With a background in teaching English Bethany is passionate about communication and in giving young people the skills the need to understand the world around them. As Head of Education and English Lead at Wessex Lodge School Bethany has worked to create a curriculum that supports students of every stage in making good progress and being able to access future opportunities. The students that we work every day deserve the absolute best from their teachers and as a member of SLT Bethany feels strongly about enabling staff to provide this. Bethany has since taken up her role as Assistant Headteacher based at The Ark in Frome. Caroline Stedman Head of Finance Having started my career in sales I moved over to an administrative role in a main stream school, this is where my passion for working within the education sector began. I moved to Wessex Lodge School in 2019 and haven’t looked back. The amazing team at the school have supported me to learn new skills and allowed me to grow not just in my career, but as a person too. My role has since evolved from Senior Administrator into the School Business Manager. This new role keeps me very busy, from HR, Finance, budgets and fleet support, to supporting the lunch and admin teams. In my role I enjoy being able to support our young people, from the ‘behind the scenes work’ arranging trips etc. to be front of house and greeting them on their arrival.
A qualified SENCO and diploma-qualified trauma-informed practitioner, Laura combines specialist expertise in SEND, emotional wellbeing and behaviour with practical experience of strengthening provision. She leads the development of consistent behaviour systems, restorative approaches and targeted interventions, ensuring pupils receive the understanding, boundaries and support needed to build positive relationships and engage in school life.
In previous roles, Laura has redesigned personal development and careers provision and led a supported internship programme, securing meaningful placements through partnerships with employers, families and support teams. This experience informs her leadership of PSHE, SMSC, life skills and careers, connecting pupils’ aspirations with practical independence and future opportunities. She also supports early career teachers as an ECT mentor.
Laura’s ambition is that every pupil experiences an education that takes their potential seriously, one that builds self-belief, broadens opportunity and equips them to shape their own future.

Home About Us What we do
What we do
At Wessex Lodge School, we are committed to raising achievement and enabling all students to achieve their full potential. We support them through a personalised, engaging, and relevant curriculum which helps to overcome a complex range of barriers to learning.
Our students are always our priority, and we constantly work to develop and improve our core knowledge and skills to support our students so that they can make a manageable and meaningful successful transition to work, college, and adult life. The environment we provide will give students a structured and supportive place where they feel safe enough to take responsibility for their actions.
We will work tirelessly to ensure that your child has the very best opportunities to progress in their learning and in their emotional development. We invest in the best resources to enhance the school’s learning environment and ensure that staff receive a high level of training, so we are more able to help your child succeed in school and in life.
We know from talking to parents and carers that when their child joins us it is often at a point when they feel beaten by the experiences they have had trying to find the right educational placement for their child. Families often feel like they have been torn apart by an education system that does not meet the needs of their child. At Wessex Lodge we put every child at the forefront of our thinking. We design a personalised educational experience that will re-engage, motivate and excite our students. Our carefully considered nurturing support, supported by our Elsa and Clinical team and Trauma Informed approach helps the students to grow in confidence and begin to dream big again. As a result of our interventions the wounds that families have received can begin to heal and everyone can thrive and flourish.
We have developed a high level of specialism in working with students with SEMH, ASC and attachment difficulties and a range of learning difficulties. We have helped the most disaffected and disengaged students begin to make outstanding educational and emotional progress. We do not give up on our students and will do everything we can to make education work for them. We are passionate in helping our families and will go the extra mile to ensure that they feel listened to and supported.
When a child joins our school, we expect that:
· They will achieve the best results and qualifications. We know that this is different for every student. Many of our students will gain Functional Skills and GCSE results. Many will complete vocational qualifications and foundation skills. Many students will attend relevant work placements and gain qualifications and essential experience that will position them better for life after school.
· They will progress outstandingly well across a broad range of subjects including literacy and numeracy.
· They will develop emotional resilience and a better social awareness so they can begin, and continue, to experience success and be successful in society when they leave Wessex Lodge School.
· At Wessex Lodge School we know that there is no magic wand that can be waved to make things better for our students and their families. Instead, we offer hard work, dedication, the best trained professionals, support out of school and an assurance that we will do all that we can to ensure the best outcomes for your child.
We aim to achieve high quality outcomes for students by:
· Reducing or removing their barriers to learning.
· Developing their ability to communicate and interact with others appropriately.
· Working to foster their ability to be flexible and adapt to change.
· Encouraging pupils to positively manage any difficulties or periods of dysregulation.
· Working with them to develop their self-esteem, independence, and their ability to have positive and constructive relationships with others.
· Ensuring every student receives a broad, balanced, and relevant curriculum that meets each of their needs and gives the right level of challenge and support.
· Making available a wide range of therapies to help students overcome their difficulties and to help them reach their full potential.
· Keeping them safe and protecting their welfare, and through the broader curriculum developing their ability to keep themselves safe.
· Helping pupils to explore how they think and behave through a variety of therapies, including, but not limited to, psychological, mental health, SALT, OT, CBT, person centred approaches, supported by the Elsa and Clinical team.
· Committing to the principle that every student, regardless of their ability, race, gender, cultural and religious background, or immigration status will receive the highest quality of education we can provide.
· Working together with their parents/carers and other professionals as an effective multi-disciplinary team.
Please never hesitate to call, email or write should you want to know any more about our wonderful school.
We make a difference… alumni talk at Wessex Lodge careers day;
“From starting at the school to this point where I am now, without the school I never would’ve made it, I never would’ve passed my GCSE. My mum didn’t think I’d pass my GCSE at all and it’s really difficult especially her position because she wants to see her son succeed but having to deal with the troubles that I had in primary school she just didn’t think I could do it, but at this school where they had the teachers the training and the ability to be able to help me in the ways that I needed to be helped it gave me security. It gave me a platform to stand on and without it I never would’ve became the person who I am now.”
© OFG Education 2026

Home Our Approach Curriculum
Curriculum
Our curriculum is underpinned by Thrive and our Trauma Informed approach. We offer a broad, bespoke curriculum to our students.
Our curriculum is divided into Pathway 1 – preparing to learn, Pathway two- ready to learn, Pathway three – interdependence (accredited courses). Our offer includes Functional Skills and GCSE for core subjects, D of E accreditations and Science accreditations (Pre GCSE Levels). We also offer PE, Outdoor Education and Forest School, Animal Care, Home Cooking Skills, Thrive individualised specific timetabled sessions, and an excellent PSHE/RSE provision. In addition to a very broad curriculum offer we deliver Computing, Art & design, Food technology, Humanities, Design technology, Music Therapy and AQA Unit Awards.
Our school day begins at 8:30 for staff briefing with students arriving on site at 9:30 a.m. and finishing the school day at 3:00 p.m. Our day is divided into 6 sessions, including a tutorial and end of day catch up.
Lunch time is between 1245 till 1310. We run core subjects in the morning across all 3 sites and then our hook subjects in the afternoon. With three vastly different sites we are able to deliver a broad curriculum based on Student pathways and student subject interests.
Students have access to safe spaces and safe adults on all sites, and PSHE intervention, including I and E (Inclusion and engagement) intervention can occur in real time or reparative time. De-brief for staff occurs after all students have left site, for staff to discuss and handover for the day.
© OFG Education 2026

Home News & Events Residential 2024 Devon
Residential 2024 Devon
On Monday 1st July we ventured to the beautiful place of Devon, all the students were really excited about going away with their peers but also having the opportunity to experience new activities.
We arrived at Beam House, the students went to their rooms picked the beds, Myles at this point was trying to do pull ups on the bunk beds whilst the other boys were more concerned about what was for dinner. The girls unpacked and tried out the other 8 beds out that they had in the room. The adults by this point needed a siesta from the amount of excitement that they all had.
On the first night the students settled into camp well, they all tried out the showers and played board games in the dinning hall. Note to all – do not play UNO with Alfie, he ends up giving someone 20 plus cards on round one of playing. The students were all connecting and just enjoying having a late night. Then came the 6:00 wake up calls, to the boy’s disappointment breakfast wasn’t that early but they were greeted by Corry who took up for a full English breakfast as well as an all you can eat buffet. Phil needed to stay away from the sausages!!
During the day the students participated in various activities including abseiling. They all had a go either going down the wall or just walking up the tower – they all showed tremendous resilience and teamwork during this session. Kingsleigh was brave enough to be the first to abseil which took courage!
Friday morning, we were woken up at 1:20am by the delightful sound of the fire alarm, in which all the students thought it was Kingleigh’s alarm clock of Glastonbury which made everyone laugh! We then ventured to surfing, they all looked like something from the avengers but with surf boards! The instructor was so impressed that they could all stand up on the surfboard without falling off and they showed great empathy towards each other.
The students had an amazing experience, not just because of the place but because of the people that they went with, they grabbed every opportunity with an open mind. All of them brought something to the camp which made it extra special!
A massive thank you for all the staff that was involved and behind the scenes in making it happen for these incredible young people!
Keep your eyes peeled for another residential in 2025.
© OFG Education 2026
